correctness.rationale: The proof symmetrizes *every* feasible kernel by a subgroup acting transitively on vertices, using convexity of \(\|P-J/N\|_2\). Invariant kernels have exactly \(d\) edge values and capacity \(\sum_i(1-1/q_i)x_i\le1\). The tensor eigenspaces have exact subset-sum eigenvalues \(1-\sum_{i\in S}x_i\), so SLEM is \(\max\{1-\min_i x_i,\sum_i x_i-1\}\). Since \(\min_i x_i\le1/C\) and \(\sum_i x_i\ge d\min_i x_i\), a sharp one-variable lower bound results, attained with every \(x_i\) equal to \(\min\{2/(d+1),1/C\}\). Both holding phases, invariant uniqueness and the \(K_2\square K_Q\) comparison follow from equality constraints. The packaged rational verifier exercises finite cases only; the universal claim is proved symbolically.

The arXiv:0709.0955 primary text Sections 3.2 and 3.3.3 treat Cartesian-product spectra and equal-size Hamming graphs; the explicit single-weight edge-transitive answer does not handle two or more different coordinate clique sizes, where different edge-direction weights are essential. No inspected primary text or nearby published research record states the closed all-dimensional heterogeneous SLEM/weights/holding transition. Distinct-support and distinct-invariant records are not dominating results. This is a qualified best-knowledge assessment, not a guarantee against unindexed literature.

value.rationale: This is a complete closed optimization/classification across arbitrary dimension and all heterogeneous coordinate alphabet sizes, a natural family of product-state sampling and consensus networks. The theorem identifies the unique invariant spectral-rate-balancing design, its exact loop-to-loopless threshold and a parameter-unbounded penalty for naively using one edge probability: \(K_2\square K_Q\) achieves contraction \(1/3\) optimally versus \(1-2/Q\) under identical edge weights. The contribution is more than a finite toy calculation or small gain and directly controls the spectral relaxation proxy.
